description:
An easy-to-use Windows manager for personal game servers.

Synix Control Panel installs, configures, updates, monitors, and backs up personal game servers from one Windows application.
v1.0.27 adds customizable themes, remote server management, more interface languages, stronger connection security, and improved resource monitoring.

Added light and dark modes with Synix, Graphite, Ocean, Forest, Violet, and Sand themes. Users can choose accent colors and rounded or square controls. Appearance changes apply immediately and are remembered between sessions.

Expanded interface translations from 27 to 37 language options by adding Bulgarian, Croatian, Catalan, Slovak, Slovenian, Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Malay, and Filipino. Improved language selection, translated layouts, and fallback handling.

Added optional remote management through manager.synix.info. Pair and approve a computer in Synix to view server status, player counts, uptime, and resource usage from a web browser. Supported actions include starting, stopping, restarting, updating, creating backups, and restoring backups. The paired computer must remain online with Synix running.

Added protected remote console commands for supported Minecraft Java and Bedrock servers. Console access requires additional account verification and expires automatically. Game-server files and backups remain on the paired computer.

Added website password recovery from an already approved, paired computer. Recovery uses a temporary, single-use password and preserves existing authenticator or passkey requirements. The recovery button is available directly on the Remote manager settings card.

Strengthened remote connections with signed requests, short-lived credentials, protection against reused requests, and additional ownership and permission checks. Unpairing removes remote access without deleting local servers or backups.

Expanded resource monitoring with live process trees, linked launcher and console processes, and computer CPU, memory, and network readings for remote management.

Fixed reconnect messages showing internal translation codes instead of identifying the running server that Synix reconnected to. Reduced empty space in Privacy & Security settings cards.

Added optional active-session sharing for the Synix website. It is enabled by default, can be disabled in Privacy & Security, and respects an existing disabled preference.

Updated the application and installer license with official download sources, active-count disclosures, and remote-access privacy information. Clarified that remote pairing does not transfer when moving Synix to another computer.

Updated Synix to .NET 11. Official standalone and MSI releases include the required runtime, so users do not need to install .NET separately.
